content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to install [product_name] [version_no] on my laptop (Windows 10, 64-bit). I've installed the main application but now I need to set up the USB driver 'CP210X USB to UART'. The installation completes, but when I try to run the driver to install the INF files, I get this error message: 'The specified INF files could not be copied. Please check your installation and try again.' Does anyone know a solution?

Hello, Did you begin the installation with administrator privileges? Are you sure the USB driver is required for your setup? If not, you could skip this step (mainly necessary with [product_name] [version_no] units). Hope this assists.

Thanks for your reply. Yes, I started the installation as admin. I do need the USB driver, as some of my installations use [product_name] [version_no] (connected via USB cable), while others use [product_name] [version_no] (connected through Ethernet).
Try installing the driver directly from the manufacturer's website. You can find it at this link. Regards, [user_name]
The problem is solved! I disabled driver signature enforcement following the details here: [url].

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered trouble installing the USB driver (CP210X USB to UART) for use with [product_name] [version_no] on Windows 10 (64-bit). Although the software installation was successful, an error appeared during INF file installation. The underlying cause was Windows driver signature enforcement, which blocked the driver. Attempts to resolve included running as admin and checking for the correct driver source. The issue was ultimately resolved by turning off driver signature enforcement.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a straightforward installation process, including all necessary software and drivers on Windows 10, to enable hardware communication for programming and managing [product_name] [version_no] controllers.
